english.title: Aggravated vehicle taking - ( driver did not take ) and dangerous driving
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing that a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), had been taken without the consent of the owner or other lawful authority, drove the said vehicle, and after the vehicle was unlawfully taken and before it was recovered, the vehicle was driven dangerously

(A)_[on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ROAD AND LOCATION..).]_
(B)_[on roads, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ROADS AND THEIR LOCATIONS..).]_
(C)_[in a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PUBLIC PLACE AND ITS LOCATION..).]_

(D)_[There were no other additional aggravating factors]_
(E)_[Additional aggravating factors were **(..SPECIFY THE FACTORS..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12A of the Theft Act 1968.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This wording is for use ONLY were the defendant was a 'SUBSEQUENT DRIVER' - for the 'initial taker' see H4391 and 'being carried on' see H4393.
(ii) If more than one of options A to C applies, the wording must be adapted to include all aggravating features.
(iii) See also H4386, H4385, H4387, H4483, H4484 and H4485 for other aggravated vehicle taking wordings relating to a 'subsequent driver'.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment.

Obligatory disqualification and endorsement.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points - only if special reasons apply.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
